entries.notes: AccountsList.jsx:54 useFirestoreCollection(ACCOUNTS_COLLECTION) — whole collection, all filtering/counting client-side. DECISIONS #102 §9 violation. FIRST HALF QUEUED (#1137): Account entity + account.index list, the program's first real definitions. Enum labels sourced from domain/constants rather than a second copy; identity claims no reference number because an Account has none; tags render but claim no operator until the index exists; landing view is recently-viewed. Exposed and fixed a real defect - requiredIndexes() emitted ASC/DESC into output meant to be pasted into firestore.indexes.json, where only ASCENDING/DESCENDING is accepted, so every demand compared unequal against all eight existing declarations and would have failed the deploy of its own fix. SECOND HALF IS NOT A PURE LIST MIGRATION - OPEN QUESTION: /customers renders portfolio summary cards (total/active/prospect/inactive/archived counts) computed client-side over the WHOLE accounts collection, plus a tag facet built the same way. Those are AGGREGATES, not list rows: bounding their input makes the counts mathematically false while presenting them as complete - the same class as X-INVENTORY-ANALYTICS-AGGREGATE. Migrating the table to bounded paging while leaving the cards reading everything would keep the unbounded read and add a second one. Resolving it needs either an authoritative count source or a decision to reframe/remove the cards, which is a product decision a read-shape rule does not authorize. RESOLVED by Owner portfolio ruling and delivered (#1138): cards KEPT, fed by getAccountPortfolioSummary - a server-side count over the complete scope, authorized with the existing account.record.read rather than a new capability, not materialized. total is counted INDEPENDENTLY of the per-status counts so the difference surfaces as `unclassified`, which is how a legacy title-cased status is reported rather than vanishing from four categories that then fail to add up. The whole-collection subscription is REMOVED, not kept alongside. Tag facet, relationship facet and global search deferred as future governed work - each was built from a client-side full-collection scan and rebuilding any of them from a page would present partial data as complete. Also corrected a defect in the merged definition: relationshipType (singular ENUM) is not a stored field; accounts carry relationshipTypes, an array, now typed with the new ENUM_SET field type.

entries.notes: workOrderService.ts:90 onSnapshot(collection(...)) with no where() — unbounded, client-filtered. GATE B DEFINITIONS MERGED (#1141), and the point of running a non-CRM entity early is that it found three things. (1) A numeric enum could never validate: object keys are strings, so comparing enumLabels[1] against the number 1 reported every numeric enum as mislabelled - Work Order priority is stored 1..4. Both label checks now normalize to strings and the #1093 rule survives. (2) No canonical Work Order STATUS vocabulary existed; the only complete map lived inside DispatchSchedulingWorkspace. domain/workOrderStatus.js now holds it and that workspace imports it, so no user-visible copy changed. Deliberately not merged with controlTower's map, which describes what a panel is FOR at each stage rather than naming the state. (3) Three optional filters cost SEVEN composites and two cost three, so priority stays a column rather than a filter until someone accepts the cost - the derivation making a tradeoff visible instead of silently under-declaring. Identity is the reference number with NO name field: the complaint is optional, and an identity field that is frequently absent licenses a fallback to the document id. Unlike Customers, no aggregate blocker was found - the surface shows a queue, not netted totals. SURFACE FINDING: there is no /work-orders LIST route. Work Orders are reached through operational BOARDS - Dispatch, Control Tower, Dispatcher Board - and a detail page, and all three boards share one unfiltered collection listener that they bucket, group and search entirely client-side. So 'migrate the Work Orders list' presumes a list that does not exist. The boards are the same class of problem as the Customers portfolio cards, not the same class as its table: a board showing the first fifty work orders bucketed into columns presents a partial queue as the whole one, which is worse than the unbounded read it would replace. Gate B's actual purpose is unaffected - the definitions validated the contract against a non-CRM entity and found three defects. What is unresolved is which surface consumes workOrder.index.

The safety argument is an asymmetry: application code registers behavior, definitions only select from what was registered, so widening tenant configuration can never widen what code may run. Re-registering an id THROWS - a silent overwrite could shadow a governed action with a weaker capability under the same id, an authorization gap with no diff looking wrong. Nothing populates the registries yet; that arrives with the runtime. CI REPAIR: the Metadata Contracts failure was MY conflict resolution. The two step blocks shared one trailing 'working-directory' line, so merging both left a step without it and that step ran from the repo root, where its test file does not exist. The resolver's guard missed it because it checked each suite was NAMED, not that it was RUNNABLE - the same blind spot as the access generator's round-trip check. The resolver now parses the YAML and rejects any test step lacking a working-directory.

entries.title: Shared contract source of truth
entries.nextAction: Merged to origin/main; verified by mergeSha
entries.notes: The audit decided this rather than leaving it open: there is no root package.json and no workspace tooling, the functions tsconfig scopes rootDir and include to src, and firebase deploy zips only the functions directory - so a genuine shared module means new workspace tooling plus deploy-packaging risk, against a Functions pipeline that is manual and has no CI gate. Generated mirror plus parity CI carries zero deploy risk and is repo-native. GAP FOUND: governedBusinessRoles.ts and shadowParityHarness.ts are mirrored with NO cross-file parity test - and governedBusinessRoles.ts is exactly the file PR #1100 would have to change in lockstep. UPDATE: the parity-coverage half is done (PR #1104) - governedBusinessRoles.ts and shadowParityHarness.ts are now enforced, and the CI path filter now includes field-ops-app-vite/src/access/** so a client-only edit actually triggers the guard. Remaining: single authored source plus generated mirror, so humans and agents stop hand-maintaining two copies at all. DESIGN FINDING (2026-08-17): diffing the mirror pairs shows the ONLY difference is the self-referential cross-reference line - each copy names the OTHER copy's path - plus the wrap point of the sentence containing it, since the two paths differ in length. That yields two candidate designs, and the choice should be made deliberately rather than by whichever is easier to script. (A) Make the cross-reference path-independent, e.g. 'mirrored at the peer access/ module of the same name'. The pairs then become byte-identical, the generator collapses to a plain copy, the parity check collapses to byte equality, and the existing comment-paragraph/CRLF normalization stops being load-bearing. Touches the header of every mirrored module, comments only. (B) Keep the paths and have the generator substitute and re-wrap. Preserves existing text but makes the generator responsible for comment reflow, which is fragile and is exactly what the current normalization exists to tolerate. (A) removes the difference; (B) automates around it. Recommend (A), but it edits several headers and should be a deliberate call, not a side effect of building a script. RESOLVED via design (A): the self-referential pathname was REMOVED from the canonical bodies rather than automated around, so the bodies are byte-identical, generation is a copy and verification is byte equality. Six pairs synced. permissionCatalog.ts excluded (client copy carries ~30 lines of independently abbreviated comments; regenerating is behavior-neutral but deserves its own review in the most authorization-sensitive file) and parityFixtures.ts excluded (genuine firebase-admin vs firebase SDK import difference, not an artificial one).

entries.title: Bounded-read remediation across list-exempt surfaces
entries.nextAction: Merged to origin/main; verified by mergeSha
entries.notes: EXEMPT from the list runtime is NOT exempt from the scale rule, and collapsing those two exemptions would quietly bless unbounded reads on boards, calendars, dashboards and wizards. Prior art to generalize: useInstalledEquipmentPage.js, reorder request history paging, and subscribeAssignedWorkOrders with its where plus limit(100). SPLIT REQUIRED (ruling section 4). Two different problems were being tracked as one. PURE LIST reads - accounts, technicians, warehouses, suppliers, transfer orders, parts - can simply be bounded and paged, because a page of rows is an honest page of rows. AGGREGATE reads - the Operations dashboard's netted availableStock, consumption and technician-volume rollups, and getInventoryAnalytics - cannot, because a page of inputs yields a false total. blockers.requiredDecision: Either (a) the board scope is genuinely bounded - a date window, an assigned-technician set, or open-states-only - which makes a bounded read HONEST rather than partial, or (b) the board needs a governed aggregate for its column counts the way Customers did, or (c) a new /work-orders list route is created for the browsing case and the boards keep their own scope. (a) is likely correct for a dispatch board, which nobody reads beyond the current week - but what that window IS is a business decision.

entries.notes: Recorded on discovering that workOrder.index has no consuming surface. The definitions are merged and correct; what is missing is the answer to which surface should consume them.

entries.title: Record provenance platform invariant
entries.nextAction: Merged. The origin seam (createdVia/initiatedBy/sourceExecutionId) awaits reconciliation with the audit event architecture before anything writes it.
entries.notes: Server-authoritative: no writeCapability, because a client-supplied timestamp or actor is a CLAIM - any caller who can write the record can write the claim. Append-only records get two fields, not four: emitting updatedAt on an issued invoice implies a mutation path that must not exist. Synonyms (creationDate, lastModified) are REJECTED - legacy storage is handled with storagePath, never a second name in the standard vocabulary. Exemptions for caches/locks/transient state require a stated reason, so an exemption is a decision rather than a gap. Deliberately does NOT duplicate the audit event architecture: provenance is current state, audit is each material mutation, and reconstructing history from updatedBy makes the last writer look like the only writer.

entries.title: Unified EOS query model (shared dependency)
entries.nextAction: Merged. Automation v1, EQL v1 and Bulk Data v1 are unblocked; migrating the list runtime onto the AST is a separate slice.
entries.notes: RECORDED AS A SHARED DEPENDENCY so it is not rediscovered independently by Lists, Reports, Automation, EQL and AI. List filters, saved views, the report builder, automation conditions, EQL, AI-generated queries and the admin visual builder converge on ONE governed query AST, then one pipeline: metadata validation, authority validation, queryability validation, index validation, planner, governed execution. Independent query semantics per feature is how six subsystems end up disagreeing about what a filter means. Must ABSORB the existing governed report creator rather than run beside it, and must NOT collapse the board-scope contract into list pagination - a board returns a complete working set or admits it cannot, which is a different promise from a page. BUILT: makeQuery/comparison/group/traversal AST plus validateAgainstMetadata -> validateAuthority -> validateQueryability, stopping at the first refusal. Stage ORDER is deliberate: reporting a denial for a field that does not exist tells a caller something false about their access, and reporting a missing index for an unauthorized query leaks the shape of data they cannot see. A field a viewer may not READ cannot be FILTERED on either, because a predicate over a hidden field leaks its values by binary search. Traversal authority is the RELATED entity, not this one. An empty IN is REFUSED rather than resolved by whichever backend runs it - ambiguous by convention, and six consumers guessing separately is what this model prevents. completeness PAGE/COMPLETE/AGGREGATE keeps the board promise distinct from list paging rather than collapsing it.

entries.title: Automation Architecture v1
entries.nextAction: Design after the unified query model - automation CONDITIONS are queries
entries.notes: Visual flow builder to declarative model to governed execution engine. WHEN/IF/THEN over REGISTERED actions only. Core invariant: admins may COMPOSE approved business capabilities; automation may not INVENT executable authority - an engine that could write arbitrary fields is a database backdoor with a friendly interface. No JavaScript, Python, SQL writes, eval or executable metadata reaches an administrator. Operability is part of v1 rather than a later hardening pass: dry-run, execution audit, correlation identity, loop and recursion prevention, retry/idempotency, draft/active lifecycle, versioning. The canonical incident is A changes status triggering B changing status triggering A, and causality is cheaper to design than to diagnose.

entries.title: EQL / Governed Query Architecture v1
entries.nextAction: Design the surface syntax AFTER the shared query model it compiles into
entries.notes: SQL-INSPIRED because those concepts are already understood by developers, analysts, admins, BI users and AI - but claiming NO ANSI compatibility, exposing no Firestore, and never implying relational joins EOS cannot execute honestly. References stable systemNames so a label change cannot break a query. Relationships traversed by registered name, never by reconstructing storage join predicates. READ-ORIENTED: no UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT/DROP/ALTER - bulk modification is query, preview scope, choose a registered governed action, validate authority, execute, audit. AI gets no bypass: AI-generated queries pass the same validation as human-authored ones, which is the point of having one contract.

entries.title: Bulk Data Architecture v1 (import + export)
entries.nextAction: Design after the query model - an export IS a governed query with a different sink
entries.notes: Core invariant: BULK CHANGES SCALE, NOT AUTHORITY - a bulk operation cannot do what its initiating actor could not do one record at a time. Identity uses recordId, business reference or approved alternateKey; NEVER a mutable human label. 0 matches create-if-permitted, 1 match update, more than 1 is an INTEGRITY FAILURE and never a guess. Dry run mutates nothing. EXPORT AUTHORITY IS A HARD BOUNDARY: if a user may read 4,200 records and 8 fields, Export All means all within THEIR authorized scope - not 4,201 records, not a ninth field - and the server-side job enforces it, because UI hiding is not enforcement. Export modes are distinct (human/update/integration/template/audit) and display values are not machine values, so a round-trip cannot corrupt an authoritative value. Every export produces an immutable audit record including the EFFECTIVE authorized scope, and export authority may never exceed read authority though policy may later make it stricter.

entries.title: Admin metadata configuration / page designer
entries.nextAction: Design after entities are defined - there is nothing to configure until there is metadata to configure
entries.notes: Admins configure through BUSINESS concepts, not Firestore/React/JSON/source. Field creation exposes friendly choices that EOS translates into the governed contract; systemName is proposed from the label, correctable before creation, stable after. Semantic documentation (purpose, businessMeaning, ownerDomain, sourceOfTruth) is OPTIONAL - requiring it to create a simple field produces documentation written to satisfy a validator. Page metadata REQUESTS presentation and never grants authority: editable applies only if the field is updateable AND the viewer holds write authority AND the command permits it AND lifecycle state allows it. OPERATIONAL pages are protected - layout flexibility may not remove Lifecycle/Readiness/Blockers/Next Actions, because placement flexibility and composition invariants are separate concerns and only one is negotiable. Preview must evaluate REAL governed authority; a preview with its own permission model reports what the builder thinks rather than what the platform will do. Publication must fail where the backend cannot honestly support the declared behavior.

entries.title: Contact write paths do not agree on provenance
entries.nextAction: Converge the three contact write paths on createdAt/createdBy/updatedAt/updatedBy
entries.notes: Found while defining the Contact entity. createContact writes NEITHER timestamp; the CSV importer writes createdAt/updatedAt and no actor; only the sandbox seed writes createdBy/updatedBy. The provenance invariant says every durable business record carries createdAt/createdBy, and contacts are durable business records. The metadata definition deliberately does NOT declare the fields, because declaring them would assert data absent from most existing documents - the remediation is a write-path change plus a backfill decision, not a metadata claim. Backfilling historical documents is a data question and may be protected.

entries.title: Sales Order has no business reference; its header renders a document id
entries.nextAction: Implement SO-YYYY-###### numbering, the entity referenceField, the header fix, and inert migration tooling
entries.notes: Found while scouting Sales Order for definition. The entity cannot declare a referenceField because none is stored, and declaring nameField would be worse - there is no name either. Until this is decided the Sales Order definition would have to declare an identity of NEITHER kind, which is exactly the condition that licenses a surface to fall back to the document id. RESOLVED AT PRODUCT LEVEL (Owner ruling 2026-08-17): the document-id-as-label pattern is NOT accepted. Sales Order gets a real immutable business reference, SO-YYYY-######, joining the approved family beside WO- and OPP-. salesOrderNumber is STANDARD/STRING/immutable/unique; alternateKey is evaluated separately rather than assumed from uniqueness. Generation is server-authoritative and concurrency-safe, never derived from the document id and never inferred from the Opportunity, Account or Work Order - the Sales Order has its own identity. LEGACY RECORDS FAIL HONESTLY: a record without a number renders a neutral reference-unavailable state, because a missing business reference is not permission to display a record id.

entries.title: Backfill salesOrderNumber onto legacy Sales Orders
entries.nextAction: Tooling repo-complete and INERT; production execution requires the established protected authorization

blockers.reason: Assigning business references to existing production Sales Orders mutates production data
blockers.requiredDecision: Owner authorization to execute the migration against production, after a dry run reports the affected record count and any collisions.

governing: Owner Sales Order identity ruling sections 5-7
entries.notes: Deliberately SEPARATE from the creation path, so future correctness does not wait on historical cleanup: new Sales Orders get numbered the moment the code activates. Tooling requirements are deterministic, idempotent, dry-run capable, collision-detecting, preserving recordId and existing relationships, emitting auditable evidence, and safe under rerun. Where historical creation timestamps are authoritative they may set the year; where ordering CANNOT be established reliably, references are assigned by an explicitly documented deterministic policy rather than pretending to reflect a historical sequence that no evidence supports.

entries.title: Equipment stores epoch-number timestamps and no actor
entries.nextAction: Determine the actual stored semantics first, then converge future governed writes
governing: Owner Sales Order identity ruling section 12
entries.notes: Found while scouting Equipment for definition. The equipment collection carries createdAt/updatedAt as NUMBERS (epoch millis, per the Rules type check) and has NO createdBy/updatedBy at all - unlike parts and equipment_models, which carry the full four as Firestore Timestamps. Two rules apply. First, determine the actual stored semantics before presenting anything: reinterpreting an epoch number as a Timestamp to match the standard presentation would misread the data rather than describe it. Second, if legacy storage must stay compatible, that is exactly what the systemName/storagePath separation is for - the standard vocabulary keeps its names and the mapping absorbs the difference. Historical actor backfill requires evidence; UNKNOWN is preferable to an invented actor.
